336: Dorothy Wellesley (1889-1956), English poet and friend of Yeats since
1935·
336.14-16: in Greek mythology, the Furies are the Erinyes, avenging spirits
who punish wrongs, especially those done to kindred. Yeats apparently draws
on Jane Ellen Harrison's Prolegomena to the Study of Greek Religion, 3rd ed.
 (1922), which objects to the personification of the Erinyes in Homer and their
transformation into "ministers of Justice" in Heraclitus. Yeats may have taken
the detail of the torches from Harrison's description of the Semnae.
